title: Nvidia’s first big move after Jensen Huang’s exit targets national security
lede: Nvidia set up a standing board committee for national security, export control compliance and trade risk, its first major move under interim CEO Colette Kress after Jensen Huang stepped down.

points: Director Suzanne Nora Johnson chairs it, with Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri as members; it meets at least once a quarter.
Nvidia's existing national security and trade compliance teams now report to the committee, and to Kress for daily operations.
The move comes amid scrutiny of Huang's alleged ties to a suspected Chinese spy and his push to ease chip export limits.
A day earlier, the Commerce Department said it would add export rules on AI chips and data centers abroad to stop remote access from China.
It landed hours before Nvidia's third-quarter earnings call.

sections.text: The new Commerce rule targets remote access to compute located outside the US, so teams renting GPU capacity across borders should expect tighter compliance checks from providers.
